brief_text: a 1 kg ball dropped onto one end of a seesaw throws a 100 g ball resting on the other end at least 50 cm above where it started

usage.text:
A 1 kg ball falls about 2 m onto the raised end of a 2.1 m seesaw. A 100 g ball sits in a stop-block lip on the lowered end. A hinge limit halts the plank after 0.6 rad of rotation, and the small ball flies off.

Rough estimate:
- **Impact:** the weight hits at about 6 m/s. If it stays with the plank on impact, angular momentum gives about 4.8 rad/s.
- **Gravity during the swing:** the weight's torque raises this to about 5.6 rad/s.
- **Launch:** that throws the ball at about 5.4 m/s, aimed about 17° off vertical. This should take it roughly 1.3 m above its start, well over the 0.5 m target.

```xml
<mujoco model="seesaw_catapult">
  <option timestep="0.002"/>
  <worldbody>
    <light name="sun" pos="0 0 4" dir="0 0 -1"/>
    <geom name="floor" type="plane" size="5 5 0.1" rgba="0.8 0.8 0.8 1"/>
    <geom name="pivot_post" type="box" pos="0 0 0.15" size="0.04 0.1 0.15" rgba="0.4 0.4 0.4 1"/>
    <body name="seesaw" pos="0 0 0.35" euler="0 0.3 0">
      <joint name="seesaw_hinge" type="hinge" axis="0 1 0" limited="true" range="-0.6 0"/>
      <geom name="seesaw_plank" type="box" size="1.05 0.08 0.02" mass="0.5" rgba="0.6 0.4 0.2 1"/>
      <geom name="seesaw_stop" type="box" pos="1.03 0 0.05" size="0.02 0.08 0.05" mass="0.02" rgba="0.5 0.3 0.1 1"/>
    </body>
    <body name="weight" pos="-0.85 0 2.6">
      <freejoint/>
      <geom name="weight" type="sphere" size="0.08" mass="1" rgba="0.2 0.2 0.8 1"/>
    </body>
    <body name="ball" pos="0.9378 0 0.1332">
      <freejoint/>
      <geom name="ball" type="sphere" size="0.05" mass="0.1" rgba="0.9 0.2 0.2 1"/>
    </body>
  </worldbody>
</mujoco>
```

```expect
weight touches seesaw
ball touches seesaw
seesaw reaches its lower stop
ball rises at least 0.5 m above its start
```

verdict.what_happens: The seesaw sits essentially flat and never moves more than a fraction of a degree. The ball, placed for a tilted plank, falls straight to the floor and stays there, never touching the seesaw. The weight lands on the plank at 0.66 s, nudges it against a 0.6-degree stop, bounces, slides off the end and rolls away along the floor. Nothing is thrown.
verdict.problem: The tilt and hinge range were written in radians but MuJoCo read them as degrees, so the plank was flat with a 0.6-degree range and the ball started under it instead of on it.

usage.text:
**What happened in the run:**
- **The seesaw never tilted.** MuJoCo read my `euler="0 0.3 0"` and `range="-0.6 0"` as degrees, not radians. So the plank sat almost flat at z = 0.35, and its range was only 0.6°.
- **The ball missed the plank.** I had placed it for a tilted plank, so it started below the flat plank. It fell straight to the floor and stayed there, never touching the seesaw.
- **The weight hit and rolled away.** It landed on the plank at 0.66 s and pushed it a fraction of a degree against its tiny stop. It bounced, then slid off the end and rolled away along the floor.
- **Nothing was thrown.** The brief is not met.

**Fix:** add `<compiler angle="radian"/>`. The tilt, the hinge range and the ball's position then mean what I designed: a 17° starting tilt, a 0.6 rad swing, and the ball resting against the end stop on the low end.

```xml
<mujoco model="seesaw_catapult">
  <compiler angle="radian"/>
  <option timestep="0.002"/>
  <worldbody>
    <light name="sun" pos="0 0 4" dir="0 0 -1"/>
    <geom name="floor" type="plane" size="5 5 0.1" rgba="0.8 0.8 0.8 1"/>
    <geom name="pivot_post" type="box" pos="0 0 0.15" size="0.04 0.1 0.15" rgba="0.4 0.4 0.4 1"/>
    <body name="seesaw" pos="0 0 0.35" euler="0 0.3 0">
      <joint name="seesaw_hinge" type="hinge" axis="0 1 0" limited="true" range="-0.6 0"/>
      <geom name="seesaw_plank" type="box" size="1.05 0.08 0.02" mass="0.5" rgba="0.6 0.4 0.2 1"/>
      <geom name="seesaw_stop" type="box" pos="1.03 0 0.05" size="0.02 0.08 0.05" mass="0.02" rgba="0.5 0.3 0.1 1"/>
    </body>
    <body name="weight" pos="-0.85 0 2.6">
      <freejoint/>
      <geom name="weight" type="sphere" size="0.08" mass="1" rgba="0.2 0.2 0.8 1"/>
    </body>
    <body name="ball" pos="0.9378 0 0.1332">
      <freejoint/>
      <geom name="ball" type="sphere" size="0.05" mass="0.1" rgba="0.9 0.2 0.2 1"/>
    </body>
  </worldbody>
</mujoco>
```

usage.text:
With the angles read as radians, the scene now does what the brief asks.

**What happens in the run:**
- **Setup:** the 100 g ball rests against the end stop on the low end of the seesaw, which is tilted 17°.
- **Impact:** the 1 kg weight falls about 1.9 m and lands on the raised end at 0.62 s.
- **Swing:** the seesaw swings through its 34° range and hits its lower stop at 0.73 s, turning at about 356°/s.
- **Launch:** the ball leaves the plank at about 4.8 m/s, heading up and back over the pivot.
- **Height:** the ball peaks at z = 1.54 m at 1.14 s. That is about 1.41 m above its start at z = 0.13 m, well over the 50 cm required.
- **Afterwards:** the weight rolls off onto the floor. It clips the ball once more at 1.66 s, after the ball has already peaked. The ball then lands and both roll away along the floor, and the empty seesaw tips back to its upper stop.
